answer: A collateralized bonding protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital in time-delayed escrows to access the network. Because adversaries cannot forge cryptographic staking proofs, they must incur the verifiable opportunity cost of illiquid capital per identity to sustain a tide of fake nodes. This provides a resilient haven for authentic agent settlement. However, high deposit barriers favor wealthy cartels and exclude resource-constrained edge agents.
